**Updated Understanding:**
The correct answer is C) The fur gains protons from the rod. Contact electrification between keratin (fur) and a polymer (plastic rod) is often mediated by ion transfer—specifically protonation/deprotonation of surface groups via adsorbed moisture—rather than pure electron transfer. The rod ending up negative can be described as the rod losing positive charge (protons) to the fur, leaving the rod with excess electrons and the fur more positive; thus, option C best captures the mechanism. While many textbook explanations simplify to electron transfer (option D), nuanced surface chemistry points to proton exchange being a dominant path in some conditions; Keratin side chains can accept H+ under friction/contact. Hence C.
